metadata.title: Bullying victimization, school belonging, academic engagement and achievement in adolescents in rural China_ A serial mediation model

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a contract research survey in a rural area of G Province, China, sampling one Grade 9 class per participating junior secondary school (106 schools → 106 classes) and then restricting the analytic sample to 15-year-olds resident in rural areas who completed all surveys and tests (final N=813). The manuscript does not report the use of PISA-style sampling weights or any complex survey design adjustments (e.g., school/stratum/cluster weights) in the analysis; instead, it reports standard ANOVAs, Pearson correlations, and regression-based mediation with bootstrapping implemented in IBM SPSS and PROCESS. Because the dependent variable is academic achievement operationalized as standardized PISA raw scores (z scores) and the analysis is mediation/regression rather than ML with weight-aware training, the paper provides no explicit weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply. Therefore, results should be interpreted as conditional on the sampled rural schools/classes and the analytic exclusions, rather than as population-representative estimates for all of China.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not use PISA plausible values (PV) or IRT/WLE/theta scaling; instead, it uses publicly released Chinese PISA tests and converts each student’s raw score to a z score for academic achievement. Because the dependent variable is treated as a standardized raw-score metric rather than a PV-based achievement scale, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not describe any missing-data procedure beyond excluding students who did not complete all surveys and tests, so a specific missing-data handling method is not reported in the analysis section.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were drawn from a rural area in G Province, southwestern China, consisting of 106 junior secondary schools (102 rural schools). One Grade 9 class was randomly sampled from each participating school, yielding 106 participating classes. All students in these Grade 9 classes were invited, but the analytic sample was restricted to students aged 15 (14–17 were initially eligible) who were resident in rural areas and completed all surveys and tests; students from urban areas and other ages were excluded. The PISA test was administered as a term exam by participating schools, and the final sample used in mediation analyses is N=813 (359 boys, 454 girls).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2009 the study leveraged Gender to predict predicted school belonging (β=-0, finding that This study examines how bullying victimization relates to academic achievement in 15-year-olds in rural China, using a contract survey in G Province and administering Chinese versions of PISA reading, math, and science tests as a term exam. The analytic sample comprised 813 students (359 boys, 454 girls) from 102 rural classes, restricted to rural residents aged 15 who completed all surveys and tests. The study does not train machine-learning models; instead, it uses regression-based serial mediation (PROCESS 2.1) with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) to test whether school belonging and academic engagement sequentially mediate the bullying–achievement association, separately by gender. In the full sample, bullying victimization negatively predicted school belonging (β=-0.30, p<0.001), school belonging positively predicted academic engagement (β=0.46, p<0.001), and academic engagement positively predicted academic achievement (β=0.21, p<0.01). The serial indirect effect bullying victimization → school belonging → academic engagement → academic achievement was significant in the full sample (β=-0.03, 95% CI [-0.05, -0.01]) and in boys (β=-0.02, 95% CI [-0.05, -0.005]), but not in girls, where academic engagement did not predict achievement (β=0.15, p>0.05). Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal direction), self-report measures for bullying/belonging/engagement, and lack of explicit missing-data handling beyond complete-case exclusion. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an empirical mediation/regression study rather than an ML predictive modeling paper: the manuscript reports ANOVAs, Pearson correlations, and PROCESS-based serial mediation with bootstrapped indirect effects, and it does not specify any machine-learning algorithms, training/validation procedure, or ML performance metrics. Consequently, ml_techniques is empty and main_findings is left empty because the schema requires StructuredFinding rows for distinct ML target variables, which are not present in the ML sense in this article.
